title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-08
ranking_basis: GitHub Trending daily stars gained, descending, with one clearly labeled newly created Search API discovery appended as a supplement.
ranking_explanation: The first ten entries are ordered by the daily star-gain figures displayed on GitHub Trending at capture time. The eleventh entry was created within the last two days and found by GitHub Search; its lifetime stars are not a daily gain and it is not interleaved into the Trending order.
global_caveat: Trending star gains and total stars are point-in-time values. GitHub Search exposes current totals, not historical daily deltas. The supplemental repository's star count is lifetime total, not a daily gain. No prior-window comparison was gathered, so no Notable Shifts section is claimed.

themes.title: Reusable agent skills and workflows
themes.content: Four entries package agent expertise as installable or reusable skill collections: Cloudflare's audit workflow, Matt Pocock's composable engineering skills, Google product skills, and Anthropic's public skills. The strong daily gains on this cluster make it the clearest shared signal.

themes.title: Agent execution surfaces and longer-context workflows
themes.content: OpenMausBot puts multiple locally run agents into a desktop chat workflow, while billion-context targets compression for long-running agent sessions. Together they point from prompt libraries toward persistent, tool-using applications and context management.

themes.title: Security automation and identity search
themes.content: Cloudflare's structured multi-stage code-audit skill and Sherlock's cross-network username search are distinct security-adjacent utilities that both gained substantial daily attention.

themes.title: Developer productivity tooling
themes.content: Zed's multiplayer editor and Ruff's fast Python linting/formatting represent established, practical developer tools alongside the agent-centric projects.

themes.title: Observability and infrastructure
themes.content: Prometheus remains a high-attention infrastructure project, evidence that the daily list is not exclusively agent-focused.

themes.title: Native retro-game recompilation (fresh-repository supplement)
themes.content: The newly created Ocarina Recomp repository translates game code to C and builds locally from a user's own copy; it is a striking outlier, but its current implementation is explicitly experimental.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content:
Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-08 01:34 UTC
Scope: Daily
Date range: 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-08
Ranking basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains; one separate newly created Search API discovery is appended.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent skills and workflows dominate today's strongest GitHub momentum, led by Cloudflare's security-audit skill and two sharply rising agent applications/utilities. The mix also includes durable developer tools and one experimental retro-game recompilation project surfaced separately as newly created.

sections.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
sections.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings.
sections.content: A coding-agent security auditor that coordinates reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, and independent verification, then emits schema-checked findings and reports.
sections.why_notable: It led the daily Trending list by the displayed star-gain figure and its README documents a concrete six-phase audit and verification workflow.
sections.unique_caveat: The default branch's latest push was 2026-09-14; the strong star gain reflects attention, not evidence of a same-day code release.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A skill orchestrates isolated agents through six phases and uses explicit coverage and findings ledgers with validators.
enrichment.workflow: Map trust boundaries and coverage; hunt by ledger unit; independently try to disprove each candidate; validate structured findings; verify final claims; derive reports.
enrichment.design_pattern: Coverage-tracked, multi-agent audit with independent verification and machine-readable outputs.

sections.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
sections.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use.
sections.content: An open-source desktop chat app for managing multiple agents, each with its own personality, model, computer, and connected apps; the README describes Claude or Codex running locally under the hood.
sections.why_notable: It recorded the second-highest daily star gain in the captured Trending view and represents a more productized, multi-agent interface rather than a prompt collection.
sections.unique_caveat: The project states it is independent and not affiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI, or Manus; its README describes local agent processes, while calling the per-agent environment a cloud computer.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A TypeScript, React, and Electron desktop client presents multiple agents as chat contacts, each with its own model, personality, computer, and connected apps.
enrichment.workflow: Create or select an agent in the sidebar, chat with it, observe its work, and approve actions when needed.
enrichment.design_pattern: Multi-agent desktop cockpit with conversational, contact-like interaction and user approval points.

sections.title: sherlock-project/sherlock
sections.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks.
sections.content: A Python CLI and package that searches usernames across 400+ social networks, with options for site filtering, proxy routing, and text/CSV/XLSX output.
sections.why_notable: It had the third-largest daily star gain among the captured Trending repositories and is the clearest non-agent utility in the top three.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Python command-line tool and package loads site definitions and checks usernames across 400+ services, with concurrent network requests and multiple output formats.
enrichment.workflow: Supply one or more usernames; optionally filter sites or configure a proxy; save discovered accounts to text, CSV, or XLSX output.
enrichment.design_pattern: Extensible, data-driven OSINT search across a broad catalog of sites.

sections.title: zed-industries/zed
sections.description: A high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.
sections.content: A performance-focused, multiplayer code editor, available for macOS, Linux, and Windows; the project is written primarily in Rust.
sections.why_notable: Its 1,114 daily stars put an established editor just above the equally large engineering-skills collection, showing that this snapshot is not only new agent projects.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Rust-based high-performance editor with multiplayer collaboration; the README directs contributors to platform-specific build documentation.
enrichment.workflow: Install a platform build or follow the corresponding contributor build guide to develop Zed.
enrichment.design_pattern: Native, cross-platform editor centered on performance and collaboration.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
sections.content: A collection of small, composable engineering skills intended to work across models and agent tools, with multiple installation paths.
sections.why_notable: It is one of the strongest daily gainers and provides a counterpoint to large all-in-one agent frameworks: editable, composable skills with per-tool installation instructions.
sections.unique_caveat: The README advises choosing either the self-updating plugin route or editable skills.sh files; installing both can duplicate skills.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A set of small, composable agent skills designed to be adapted, work across models, and install into several coding-agent ecosystems.
enrichment.workflow: Install the plugin or copy editable skill files for one agent ecosystem, then adapt or update the skills as needed.
enrichment.design_pattern: Composable, model-agnostic engineering guidance rather than a process-owning framework.

sections.title: google/skills
sections.description: Agent Skills for Google products and technologies.
sections.content: A Google-maintained set of agent skills for its products and technologies.
sections.why_notable: It is another clear daily winner in the agent-skills cluster, adding a vendor-specific collection to the broader trend.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Google-maintained, installable collection of skills for Google products and technologies, including Google Cloud.
enrichment.workflow: Install with npx skills add google/skills, select skills and target agents, then update with npx skills update.
enrichment.design_pattern: Vendor-specific skill collection distributed through a shared skills installer.

sections.title: anthropics/skills
sections.content: Anthropic's public collection of agent skills.
sections.why_notable: It adds a second major AI-lab-maintained collection to the skill-repository cluster and continued gaining several hundred stars today.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A collection of self-contained skill folders, each with a SKILL.md containing instructions and metadata for Claude to load dynamically.
enrichment.workflow: Browse or install a skill so Claude can load its instructions dynamically for a specialized, repeatable task.
enrichment.design_pattern: Task-scoped instruction bundles with optional scripts and resources.

sections.title: astral-sh/ruff
sections.description: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.
sections.content: A fast Python linter and formatter implemented in Rust.
sections.why_notable: It is a practical infrastructure-level developer tool and one of two Rust projects in the Trending top ten, alongside Zed.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Rust implementation of a Python linter and formatter with pyproject.toml support and a pip installation path.
enrichment.workflow: Install Ruff with pip and use it as a Python linter and formatter, configured through pyproject.toml.
enrichment.design_pattern: A single, fast Rust tool consolidating Python linting and formatting tasks.

sections.title: prometheus/prometheus
sections.description: The Prometheus monitoring system and time series database.
sections.content: The established open-source monitoring system and time-series database.
sections.why_notable: Its presence among the larger daily gainers is a useful counterpoint to the agent-heavy profile of the list.

sections.title: ranxianglei/billion-context
sections.description: A context-compression plugin for long-running sessions and smaller context windows.
sections.content: A TypeScript plugin that claims to compress context for long-running, very large sessions and reduce token use.
sections.why_notable: It is the lowest-gain entry in the selected Trending top ten, but represents the context-efficiency side of persistent agent workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated 5x token-saving and billion-token-session scale are project claims, not independently verified benchmark results in this snapshot.

sections.title: sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp
sections.description: Ocarina of Time running natively on Windows, no emulator; built on the user's own copy, with no game files included.
sections.content: A newly created C project that translates game code to C for a native Windows build using the user's own game copy.
sections.why_notable: GitHub Search found it among the highest-starred repositories created in the last two days; it provides a useful, unusually concrete non-agent counterpoint, but has no matching Trending daily gain figure.
sections.unique_caveat: The README labels the project experimental, reports testing on one PC and only an early game region, and says users must supply their own game copy; no game files are included.

enrichment.architecture_summary: Game code is translated to C and compiled locally as a native Windows program, with graphics converted for Vulkan from the user's own game data.
enrichment.workflow: The user provides a legally obtained game image or extracted files; the local installer generates the executable and supporting artifacts.
enrichment.design_pattern: User-supplied-input recompilation rather than bundling game assets or using an emulator.

sections.source_signal: GitHub Search repositories created:2026-11-06..2026-11-08, sorted by current stars; supplemental, not part of daily Trending ranking.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Reusable agent skills are the clearest cluster: Cloudflare, Matt Pocock, Google, and Anthropic all package guidance for coding agents, while OpenMausBot and billion-context extend the pattern toward execution and long-lived context. Security automation stands out through Cloudflare's staged audit and Sherlock's username search across 400+ networks. Zed and Ruff represent Rust-powered developer tooling, while Prometheus remains a strong infrastructure counterpoint. Languages among the ten daily Trending entries: Python (3), TypeScript (2), Rust (2), JavaScript (1), Shell (1), and Go (1). The supplemental fresh repository is C.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's standout is the breadth of agent support, from reusable skills to controlled desktop workflows and context tooling. Established developer tools still draw major attention, and newly created repositories can spike quickly outside the official Trending list; treat that Search-based add-on as a separate, less comparable signal.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content:
Primary: https://github.com/trending?since=daily
Corroboration: GitHub REST repository metadata and default-branch commit endpoints for selected repos; GitHub Search API for the Cloudflare repo match and for created:2026-11-06..2026-11-08 candidates.
Method: Daily gain values come from the GitHub Trending page as captured at 2026-11-08 01:34 UTC; first ten entries are ordered by those figures. One freshly created, non-fork repository is appended based on current Search stars and recent creation/push time. Search star counts are lifetime totals; no daily delta is inferred. DeepWiki's Sherlock page was excluded because its indexed commit (2026-09-24) did not match current default-branch SHA; pinned first-party documentation was used instead. No prior-window evidence was used.
